papers.title: Reference genomes and fossils revise bat family phylogeny and biogeography.
papers.summary: Chromosome-level genome assemblies from 103 bat species across all 21 families, plus 699 morphological characters and 44 pre-Quaternary fossils, yield a revised bat phylogeny: Myzopodidae sits as earliest vespertilionoid branch, Emballonuroidea and Vespertilionoidea are sister groups, and 26 ancestral bat chromosomes are reconstructed, resolving why earlier phylogenies were misled.

papers.title: The lipidomic architecture of the mouse brain.
papers.summary: A micrometer-scale membrane-lipid atlas of the adult mouse brain, mapped across sexes and pregnancy, reveals 'lipizones' — spatial lipid territories that align with functional anatomy, partly mirror cell-type territories, capture distal axon terminals, expose a new oligodendrocyte heterogeneity axis in white matter, and adapt to physiological state, notably pregnancy.

papers.title: Insights into longevity and virus-driven adaptation from Myotis bat genomes.
papers.summary: Near-complete genome assemblies for eight Myotis bat species plus functional screens reveal distinct adaptation modes to DNA versus RNA viruses, including over-representation of positive selection in DNA-virus-interacting proteins, ancient trans-species copy-number polymorphisms of EIF2AK2/PKR, and recurrent evolution of longevity linked to selection in cancer-resistance pathways.

papers.title: Functional role of skull lymphoid structures in CNS immunosurveillance.
papers.summary: Lymphoid structures with germinal-centre-like formations exist in mouse skull bone marrow, containing follicular-helper-like T cells that drive B cell activation via CD40L, IL-21 and interferon-gamma. These cells surveil CNS-derived antigens and contribute to anti-tumor responses in brain cancer models, establishing skull marrow as a site of CNS immunosurveillance.

papers.title: Structural mechanism governing the directionality of bridge recombination.
papers.summary: Cryo-EM structures of the IS621 bridge recombinase–bridge RNA complex bound to excision DNA substrates reveal how transposon excision occurs. Unlike the bent U-shaped insertion intermediate, excision substrates are linear and bind across both bridge RNA loops, explaining the directionality control that separates excision from insertion in programmable recombination.

papers.title: Bacterial Cytochrome C Orchestrates Larval Metamorphosis Through Bioelectrical Control of Extracellular Vesicles Biogenesis.
papers.summary: Cytochrome c packaged in Gram-negative bacterial extracellular vesicles induces larval metamorphosis in marine invertebrates. Cytc maturation enhances electron transfer, supplying energy for EV biogenesis and cargo loading; docking suggests mussel larval induction via TLR4 binding, proposing a new interkingdom signaling paradigm where cytc serves as an electrogenic EV signal.

papers.title: Enrichment and Proteomic Profiling of Stromal-Associated Extracellular Vesicle Subpopulations From Arthritic Synovial Fluid by Size-Exclusion Chromatography Coupled to CD90-Directed Immunocapture.
papers.summary: A size-exclusion chromatography–ultrafiltration workflow coupled to magnetic bead CD90/Thy1 immunocapture enriches stromal-associated extracellular vesicle subpopulations from arthritic synovial fluid, offering a minimally invasive window into synovial fibroblast pathobiology for rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, validated in vitro with synovial fibroblast-derived EVs.

papers.title: Dual-Targeted M1 Macrophage Extracellular Vesicles Reprogram the Tumor Microenvironment and Enhance Natural Killer Cell Immunotherapy in Breast Cancer.
papers.summary: Dual-targeted extracellular vesicles from pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, decorated with hyaluronic acid and cyclic RGD, physically bridge NK cells to tumor cells via CD44 and integrins, deliver inflammatory cytokines and miRNAs, reprogram the immunosuppressive breast cancer microenvironment, and enhance NK cell immunotherapy in vitro and in vivo.

papers.title: Extracellular Vesicle-Bound Bacterial Toxin Pneumolysin Triggers Membrane Engagement and Damage Beyond Canonical Pore Formation.
papers.summary: At sublytic doses, host cells shed pneumolysin-laden extracellular vesicles during membrane repair. Simulations, liposome fusion assays and cryo-EM show vesicle-bound pneumolysin uses an exposed helix to engage target membranes, driving curvature, thinning and water influx beyond canonical pore formation, with plasma membrane-derived microvesicles preferentially enriched in the toxin.

papers.title: Conserved and Tissue-Specific RNA and Protein Cargos of Small Extracellular Vesicles From 120 Tissue Sites Across 34 Organs in a Single Pig.
papers.summary: A whole-body atlas of small extracellular vesicles from 120 tissue sites, four body fluids and nine gastrointestinal contents in a single pig identifies 7,995 proteins, 337 miRNAs and 105,409 transcripts. A conserved cargo core (including ANXA2, ALIX, let-7) contrasts with organ-specific cargos, and HNRNPU is implicated in hypoxia-linked cargo sorting.

papers.title: Shear Stress-Stimulated Trafficking of Endothelial Piezo1 to Splenic Capsule Boosts Spleen Contraction and Exercise Endurance.
papers.summary: Hemodynamic shear stress activates endothelial Piezo1, triggering release of medium/large extracellular vesicles that traffic Piezo1 to the splenic capsule smooth muscle, where it acts downstream of alpha-1 adrenergic signaling to boost exercise-induced spleen contraction and endurance in mice; circulating Piezo1-enriched vesicles correlate with spleen contraction in humans.

papers.title: Helicobacter pylori Outer Membrane Vesicles Engage TLR2 Through NapA to Promote Epithelial Association and Inflammatory Signalling.
papers.summary: Helicobacter pylori outer membrane vesicles preferentially associate with TLR2-expressing gastric epithelial cells and trigger NF-kappaB activation. The vesicle-associated virulence factor NapA, not urease, is the major determinant of TLR2-dependent vesicle association and inflammatory signaling, identifying a specific molecular engagement route for H. pylori OMVs.

papers.title: Extracellular Vesicle-Encapsulated Small RNAs From Clostridium Butyricum Modulate Host Intestinal Lipid Metabolism.
papers.summary: Extracellular vesicles from Clostridium butyricum enter intestinal epithelial cells and deliver miRNA-like RNAs, notably miRNA-3020179, which target PPARalpha and RXRA to suppress intestinal lipid absorption and oxidation. Supplementation prevented lipid accumulation in high-fat diet-fed mice, and deleting the miRNA abolished effects in intestinal organoids.

papers.title: Trophoblast Extracellular Vesicles Rewire Immunity: A Symptom-Relief Avenue for Recessive Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa.
papers.summary: Extravillous trophoblast-derived extracellular vesicles, modeled via the HiPEC cell line to overcome donor variability, rewire circulating monocyte responses similarly to first-trimester primary trophoblast vesicles, redirecting immunity toward repair — a candidate symptom-relief approach for recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and other inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: Crosstalk between cysteine and lysine modifications: Integrating redox and metabolic regulation.
papers.summary: Review of proximal cysteine–lysine residue pairs (<10 angstrom apart) as integration nodes for redox and metabolic regulation: local electrostatics tune residue pKa, PTM moieties transfer between residues, and covalent crosslinks form. Computational modeling plus MS-based proteomics and machine-learning PTM tools can identify candidate Cys–Lys regulatory pairs.

papers.title: LncRNA Airn preserves cardiomyocyte fatty acid oxidation to ameliorate diabetic cardiomyopathy by modulating the QKI-PPARα axis.
papers.summary: LncRNA Airn, reduced in diabetic mouse hearts, preserves cardiomyocyte fatty acid oxidation by stabilizing the RNA-binding protein QKI via the deubiquitinase PSMD14; QKI in turn stabilizes PPARalpha mRNA. Overexpression ameliorates diabetic cardiomyopathy, while PPARalpha activation rescues the lipotoxic phenotype of Airn deficiency.

papers.title: Adaptive and degenerative mitochondrial remodeling define distinct redox states in age-related macular degeneration.
papers.summary: In aged rhesus macaques with AMD-like retinal lesions, mitochondrial ultrastructure profiling and flavoprotein imaging reveal distinct redox states: normal aging shows concentric cristae and paracrystalline inclusions, while punctate deposits show fusion-associated hyperbranching; soft drusen eyes show increased metabolic heterogeneity, defining adaptive versus degenerative mitochondrial remodeling.

papers.title: Endothelial HSPA1A preserves microvascular integrity in HFpEF via HIF-1α-dependent glycolysis and NNT K1079 lactylation.
papers.summary: Endothelial HSPA1A, reduced in HFpEF, interacts with BAG2 to restrain CHIP-dependent HIF-1alpha ubiquitination, sustaining endothelial glycolysis and lactate availability. Lactate maintains NNT K1079 lactylation, preserving microvascular integrity; endothelial-targeted HSPA1A overexpression alleviates diastolic dysfunction and rarefaction in a two-hit mouse model.

papers.title: Oxidative stress and cancer: current insights and therapeutic implications.
papers.summary: Review of reactive oxygen species in cancer: moderate ROS activate KRAS, MYC and PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathways, inactivate p53 and BRCA1, remodel the tumor microenvironment through MDSCs and cancer-associated fibroblasts, and drive angiogenesis, EMT and drug resistance — while high ROS causes genomic instability and cell death, framing context-dependent therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: The Enterococcus-putrescine-hadh axis drives mitochondrial redox imbalance and endothelial barrier breakdown in aortic dissection.
papers.summary: Putrescine, elevated in aortic dissection patients and linked to disease severity, derives partly from Enterococcus via AGUA-associated metabolism. In mice, elevated putrescine impairs endothelial barrier integrity and accelerates dissection by directly binding the mitochondrial beta-oxidation enzyme HADH, driving mitochondrial redox imbalance and vascular leakage.

papers.title: Selenoprotein S associates with complexes governing membrane protein biogenesis and translation-associated processes.
papers.summary: Affinity purification with in vivo crosslinking maps the Selenoprotein S interactome: it associates with ER membrane protein insertion complexes and translation-associated processes, clarifying how this stress-response selenoprotein participates in protein quality control and linking its polymorphisms to diabetes, dyslipidemia and cardiovascular disease risks.

papers.title: NRF2-mediated ferroptosis suppression defines a cancer-specific vulnerability in tumors.
papers.summary: In a KRAS-driven lung cancer mouse model, inducible NRF2 deletion alone — without any drug — eradicates cancer cells, reduces tumor burden and prolongs survival, while non-cancerous cells tolerate NRF2 loss. Single-cell RNA sequencing with AI-based genotyping shows selective elimination of NRF2-deleted tumor cells, defining a cancer-specific vulnerability.

papers.title: CHTOP regulates the NRF2/HO-1 axis to modulate chemoresistance in colorectal cancer.
papers.summary: CHTOP promotes NRF2 transcriptional activity by recruiting the SENP3-containing complex to desumoylate NRF2, sustaining HO-1 expression and chemoresistance in colorectal cancer. Oxidative stress stabilizes SENP3, which degrades the splicing regulator p52 and relieves its suppression of CHTOP, forming a stress-sensing feedback loop.

papers.title: Chronic nitric oxide mediates dual-layer gene regulation through mRNA m(6)A positional remodeling and parallel transcriptional reprogramming.
papers.summary: Chronic nitric oxide in triple-negative breast cancer cells does not uniformly elevate mRNA m6A despite demethylase inhibition; instead it redistributes m6A — enriching the 5'UTR and coding sequence while depleting the 3'UTR — showing that m6A position, not intensity, encodes gene-regulatory information under sustained NO signaling.

papers.title: Targeting GSS-mediated glutathione synthesis: 6-Met induces oxidative stress dependent apoptosis via triggering mitochondrial bioenergetics metabolism crisis and mTOR suppression in glioblastoma.
papers.summary: 6-Met, a alkaloid from Macleaya cordata, inhibits glioblastoma proliferation in vitro and in xenograft models by targeting GSS-mediated glutathione synthesis: depleting GSH induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial bioenergetic crisis and mTOR suppression, triggering apoptosis — positioning glutathione synthesis as a metabolic vulnerability in glioblastoma.

papers.title: Elevated 5-oxoproline levels and adverse outcomes in heart failure: Association with renal cortical OPLAH loss in a multi-comorbidity model.
papers.summary: In 823 heart failure patients, serum 5-oxoproline (a glutathione-cycle metabolite) measured by LC-MS associated with worse renal function and adverse outcomes. A multi-comorbidity cardio-kidney-metabolic pig model linked 5-oxoproline accumulation to loss of renal cortical OPLAH, connecting glutathione metabolism to heart failure progression.

papers.title: Myocilin drives cardiomyocyte mitochondrial dysfunction via SLC3A2-dependent redox imbalance in heart failure.
papers.summary: Myocilin, a fibroblast-secreted protein upregulated in heart failure, drives cardiomyocyte mitochondrial dysfunction via SLC3A2-dependent redox imbalance, promoting ROS production and impaired oxidative phosphorylation. Targeting myocilin or its downstream pathway may offer viable strategies for HF mitochondrial dysfunction, a key upstream regulator previously incompletely understood.

papers.title: Inhibition of mitochondrial complex III causes selective dopaminergic neurotoxicity by redox stress in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.summary: In C. elegans, complex III-inhibiting pesticides antimycin A and pyraclostrobin cause selective dopaminergic neurotoxicity through a more-oxidized cellular environment, distinct from most established Parkinson's toxins targeting complex I. Toxicity is exacerbated in pdr-1/parkin mutants, implicating mitochondrial complex III inhibition in parkinsonian risk.

papers.title: P4HA3-mediated hydroxylation of SLC7A11 drives tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance by suppressing ferroptosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.summary: P4HA3 is upregulated in tyrosine kinase inhibitor-resistant renal cell carcinoma and drives resistance by hydroxylating SLC7A11 at P153/P161, blocking NEDD4-mediated ubiquitination and stabilizing the cystine transporter — maintaining redox homeostasis and suppressing ferroptosis. P4HA3 depletion restores sunitinib and axitinib sensitivity in vitro and in vivo.

papers.title: Systemic redox switching of transcription factors: A context-sensitive framework for cell fate decisions.
papers.summary: Proposes a 'systemic redox switching' framework resolving why transcription factors act as tumor suppressors in one context and oncogenes in another: redox regulation is network-embedded, with factors occupying homeostatic, adaptive and survival regimes connected by threshold-like, hysteretic transitions rather than discrete cysteine switches.

papers.title: Murine metabolic HFpEF is associated with altered mitochondrial substrate handling and S-nitrosylation remodeling.
papers.summary: A two-hit murine metabolic HFpEF model shows modest global proteomic changes but selective metabolomic remodeling: altered TCA cycle intermediates, increased dicarboxylic acids, and highly organized bidirectional S-nitrosylation remodeling of proteins governing fatty acid, carbohydrate and mitochondrial metabolism — defining a mitochondrial redox signature of HFpEF.

papers.title: Hypoxia drives ferroptosis resistance and immunosuppression in hepatocellular carcinoma by inducing UBASH3B-mediated glutamine metabolism reprogramming and CXCL8 expression.
papers.summary: HIF-1alpha induces UBASH3B under hypoxia in hepatocellular carcinoma; UBASH3B dephosphorylates MYBL2 at Y15, stabilizing it and reprogramming glutamine metabolism to suppress ferroptosis while promoting CXCL8-driven immunosuppression. This links hypoxia, glutamine reprogramming and ferroptosis resistance as a coordinated therapeutic resistance axis.

papers.title: Lactylation at the crossroads: Bridging metabolic rewiring and ferroptotic vulnerability in cancer.
papers.summary: Review connecting the Warburg effect, lactate accumulation, lysine lactylation and ferroptosis: lactate acts as an epigenetic precursor for histone and non-histone Kla, reshaping chromatin, while modulating lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic vulnerability — explaining why highly glycolytic tumors can remain ferroptosis-resistant despite abundant ROS.

papers.title: TDP-43 drives ferroptosis evasion by modulating PCBP1/PCBP2 axis to promote lung adenocarcinoma growth.
papers.summary: TDP-43 is upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma and correlates with poor prognosis. Silencing impairs proliferation and promotes cell death, while overexpression does the opposite. Transcriptome sequencing shows TDP-43 drives ferroptosis evasion by modulating the PCBP1/PCBP2 axis, and knockdown suppresses xenograft tumor growth in vivo.

papers.title: Nrf2-dependent reprogramming of brown adipose tissue in orthotopic breast cancer model: implications for altered systemic homeostasis.
papers.summary: In an orthotopic breast cancer model, tumor growth reprograms brown adipose tissue redox-metabolic state via NRF2. Comparing wild-type and NRF2-knockout mice across tumor sizes reveals NRF2-dependent structural, metabolic and redox remodeling of BAT, framing cancer as a systemic redox-metabolic disease affecting host tissues.

papers.title: Metalloadaptor and metallochaperone proteins reveal new chemical principles of biological metal homeostasis.
papers.summary: Review of newly discovered copper metalloadaptors and zinc metallochaperones — dedicated proteins that actively acquire and deliver transition metals across tissues, cells and proteins — establishing new chemical principles of biological metal homeostasis with implications for physiology and pathology across all kingdoms of life.

papers.title: Advances in chemoenzymatic synthesis of glycosaminoglycans and proteoglycans.
papers.summary: Advances in recombinant enzymes and biosynthetic pathways now enable defined, homogeneous glycosaminoglycan synthesis and its integration with core proteins into full proteoglycan structures, addressing the lack of unified structure-function data and opening a frontier for constructing well-defined proteoglycan glycoconjugates.

papers.title: Design of programmable molecular interfaces for synthetic biology and therapeutic applications.
papers.summary: Review of de novo protein design for synthetic biology: generative modeling, sequence design and structure prediction now enable programmable binding proteins and assemblies created from scratch, used to modulate signaling, direct targeting and organize functional architectures, though behavior prediction in complex environments remains a challenge.

papers.title: Recent discovery of new enzymes in plant natural product biosynthesis.
papers.summary: Genomics, metabolomics and structure prediction are accelerating enzyme discovery in plant natural product biosynthesis, revealing enzymes catalyzing oxidative C–C rearrangements, atypical cycloadditions, radical couplings and iterative scaffold remodeling — challenging transformations that expand biosynthetic possibilities for novel scaffolds.

papers.title: Chemical biology tools for the O-GlcNAc modification: Determining systems-level functions and druggability.
papers.summary: Review of chemical biology tools (2023-2026) for O-GlcNAc: systems-level OGT interactome maps, spatiotemporal glycosylation manipulation tools, multiplexed PTM detection, targeted modulation via nontraditional inhibitors and OGT scaffolding, and disease models — with recent OGA inhibitor phase 1/2 clinical challenges raising questions for the field.

papers.title: Discovery and engineering of enzymes for new-to-nature photobiocatalysis.
papers.summary: Photobiocatalysis merges enzymatic catalysis with photochemistry for selective radical transformations under mild conditions. Recent mechanistic advances (since 2024) in radical generation and interception within enzyme active sites guide discovery, engineering and design of enzymes for new-to-nature photobiocatalysis.

papers.title: Mapping subcellular microenvironments using oligonucleotide-directed proximity labeling.
papers.summary: Programmable DNA oligonucleotides now direct proximity labeling enzymes to specific RNAs and genomic loci, overcoming a longstanding roadblock in targeting nucleic acids. These tools reveal the molecular architecture of gene-expression compartments and provide foundations for a new generation of spatial proteomics methods.

papers.title: Icosapent ethyl activates GPR120 to improve post-myocardial infarction cardiac remodeling by suppressing CXCR3(+) inflammatory cells.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: Icosapent ethyl, a purified EPA ethyl ester, improves post-myocardial infarction remodeling in mice via myeloid GPR120 activation: better survival, preserved systolic function, reduced fibrosis and apoptosis, preserved microvascular density. Benefits are markedly attenuated in myeloid GPR120-deficient mice, with suppressed CXCR3+ inflammatory cell recruitment.

papers.title: Novel Wnt potentiators induce iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte proliferation and increase embryonic zebrafish heart size.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: Two small molecules, LRN9 and DF6, potentiate Wnt/beta-catenin signaling through a non-GSK3beta mechanism, inducing cell-cycle re-entry in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes with minimal contractile impairment versus GSK3beta inhibition. In zebrafish embryos, both compounds increase ventricular growth via cardiomyocyte hyperplasia.

papers.title: Site-specific O-GlcNAcylation of Nrf2 regulates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: NRF2 undergoes time-dependent O-GlcNAcylation after myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice and in OGD/R cardiomyocytes. Site-directed mutagenesis of S215 and S33 reveals these sites regulate NRF2 localization and transcriptional activity, and site-specific O-GlcNAcylation of NRF2 protects against I/R injury.

papers.title: PP2Acα regulates the Hippo-YAP signaling axis to promote cardiac regeneration and alleviate myocardial infarction.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: PP2Ac alpha is highly expressed in neonatal mouse hearts, declines with postnatal maturation, and is reinduced after injury. Cardiomyocyte-specific knockdown, LB100 inhibition, and gain/loss-of-function approaches show PP2Ac alpha regulates the Hippo-YAP axis to promote cardiomyocyte proliferation, cardiac regeneration and alleviation of myocardial infarction.

papers.title: TMEM175 deficiency impairs autophagic degradation and alleviates mitochondrial oxidative damage in cardiomyocytes through AMPK activation.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: TMEM175, a lysosomal proton-selective channel, shapes cardiomyocyte mitochondrial homeostasis: knockout impairs respiration and autophagic clearance under physiological conditions, yet under hydrogen peroxide stress it alleviates mitochondrial dysfunction and cell death through AMPK activation despite stalled autophagic flux at the degradation stage.

papers.title: Gfpt2 modulates fibroblast activation by glutathione metabolism.
papers.journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology
papers.summary: Loss of GFPT2, the rate-limiting hexosamine biosynthesis enzyme, shifts cardiac fibroblasts toward an activated phenotype. Untargeted metabolomics identifies glutathione metabolism as downstream, with decreased glutathione following GFPT2 loss — positioning GFPT2 as a metabolic regulator of fibroblast activation with fibrosis implications.

papers.title: Conformational stability and domain-specific structural features of tumor autoantigens regulate autoantibody epitope propensity.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: In non-small cell lung cancer, autoantigen conformational stability governs autoantibody epitope propensity: intrinsically disordered, aggregation-prone autoantigens (NY-ESO-1, XAGE-1B) elicit linear epitope responses, while thermodynamically stable soluble autoantigens drive conformational epitope recognition — informing cancer autoantibody biomarker assay design.

papers.title: Engineering a protein homodimer from a heterodimer: A chimeric DBHS protein.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A chimeric DBHS protein was engineered to homodimerize with an interface emulating the native SFPQ-NONO heterodimer. Biochemical and structural characterization confirms stable homodimer formation even in the presence of native partners, clarifying molecular determinants of DBHS partner preference across RNA lifecycle roles.

papers.title: RheoScale 2.0: Revealing the hidden roles of protein positions via substitution patterns.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: RheoScale 2.0 expands histogram-based analysis of saturation mutagenesis data to identify 'rheostat' positions — where different substitutions sample a wide range of outcomes — beyond neutral and toggle positions, revealing hidden roles of protein positions and clarifying how substitutions modulate function and stability.

papers.title: Are hyaluronic acid synthases widely encoded in fungi?
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A comprehensive in silico survey identifies 68 putative hyaluronic acid synthases across the fungal tree of life, mainly in Basidiomycota with AI-inferred candidates in Ascomycota. Shared global fold and essential residues with vertebrate and bacterial HAS suggest HA synthesis may be more widespread in fungi than appreciated.

papers.title: The assembly of tetrameric human L-lactate dehydrogenase is regulated by ionic strength, β-NADH binding, cyclic peptides, and long-chain dicarboxylates.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Human LDH-A tetramer (hLDH-5) assembly — critical for cancer metabolism — is regulated by ionic strength, beta-NADH binding, cyclic peptides and long-chain dicarboxylates. These findings illuminate monomer-to-tetramer transition control and support targeting protein-protein interactions for selective hLDH-5 inhibition.

papers.title: Adenylyl cyclase 9 as a molecular scaffold to dissect the mechanisms of membrane adenylyl cyclases.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A chimeric construct AC9-5 combines human adenylyl cyclase 9 as scaffold with the AC5 catalytic-allosteric core. Cryo-EM at 3.5 angstrom reveals the chimera bound to ATPalphaS and forskolin, partially reproducing AC5-like allosteric regulation while losing AC9's C2B-domain autoinhibition — a template for dissecting membrane AC mechanisms.

papers.title: A bacterial protein inhibitor of dUTPase disrupts zebrafish embryogenesis through a conserved active-site mechanism.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: The Staphylococcus aureus STL protein inhibits zebrafish dUTPase with 0.7 nM affinity, confirmed by crystal structure at 2.26 angstrom, biolayer interferometry and enzyme assays. This bacterial protein inhibitor disrupts zebrafish embryogenesis via a conserved active-site mechanism, establishing acute dUTPase disruption in a living vertebrate.

papers.title: Topologically complex knotted proteins are processed differentially by ATP-dependent proteases ClpXP and ClpAP.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Knotted proteins are degraded differentially by E. coli AAA+ proteases: ClpXP handles all knotted substrates regardless of topology, whereas ClpAP fails on 4_1-knotted miRFP and slows on 3_1 and 5_2 knots. Knot tail length — governing spontaneous knot movement — critically determines degradability.

papers.title: Symmetry analysis and ancestral sequence reconstruction reveal a symmetrical translocation pathway and activity determinants of ZIP metal transporters.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Internal symmetry analysis plus ancestral sequence reconstruction of ZIP metal transporters supports an evolutionary path from an ancestral 4-transmembrane protein via duplication, circular permutation and fusion into the modern 8-TM fold, revealing a continuous, symmetric metal translocation pathway and key activity determinants.

papers.title: Function within disorder: Small heat shock proteins use different functional regions to chaperone tau aggregation.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Small heat shock proteins HSPB1 and HSPB5 delay tau aggregation through distinct mechanisms dictated by their disordered N-terminal regions: HSPB1 inhibits tau aggregation under normal conditions, HSPB5 under stress such as pH acidosis. Chimeric constructs map functional regions within the intrinsically disordered termini.

papers.title: A dual gating mechanism controls target-strand cleavage in Cas12j: Implications for engineering efficient nickases.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: All-atom molecular dynamics and metadynamics (~175 microseconds sampling) reveal a coordinated dual-barrier mechanism governing target-strand accessibility in compact CRISPR Cas12j, controlled by the alpha7 helix — offering engineering targets for designing efficient nickases with controlled single-strand cleavage.

papers.title: Discovery of D-peptides that allosterically enhance SARS-CoV-2 3CLpro activity by stabilizing its monomeric state.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: D-peptides bind the SARS-CoV-2 main protease 3CLpro monomer and unexpectedly enhance catalytic activity by stabilizing the monomeric state. Lead peptide LY11 shows 117 nM affinity and sub-micromolar enzymatic activation potency, revealing an allosteric activation mechanism distinct from canonical dimerization-dependent activity.

papers.title: The Lord of the Rings: Cysteine bonds crosslink the tail of siphovirus.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Cryo-EM of siphovirus tail tube protein gp39 reveals inter-ring disulfide bonds from two cysteines per monomer, crosslinking the tail tube. Phylogenetic analysis shows ~14% of PF08813 family members carry such bonds — an evolutionary adaptation stabilizing the tubular structure, characterized alongside the disulfide-lacking homolog gp13.

papers.title: DisPhaseDB 2.0: Improved interpretation of disease-associated variants in liquid-liquid phase separation proteins with agent-accessible querying.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: DisPhaseDB 2.0 updates a database of disease-associated variants in liquid-liquid phase separation proteins with an automated, open-source Snakemake workflow that continuously fetches source data, removing update bottlenecks and adding agent-accessible querying for studying LLPS protein dysfunction in human disease.

papers.title: Two distinct alcohol dehydrogenase classes mediate bacterial 2-hydroxyethylphosphonate catabolism.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Bacterial 2-hydroxyethylphosphonate (HEP) catabolism proceeds via oxidation to phosphonoacetaldehyde, mediated by two unrelated dehydrogenase classes: homologs of the biosynthetic enzyme PhpC, and newly described enzymes. Genomic analyses define dedicated HEP degradation pathways in environmental microbes.

papers.title: Full-length brain-derived α-synuclein fibril models reveal fuzzy-coat control of peptide recognition.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Full-length, brain-derived alpha-synuclein Lewy-fold fibrils reconstructed by extending a patient-derived cryo-EM core with disordered termini show the acidic C-terminal fuzzy coat makes transient contacts with core motifs, intermittently shielding aggregation-prone ladders — shaping the surface encountered by molecular partners in Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Conformational ensembles of the disordered 4E-BP2:eIF4E complex restrained by smFRET experiments.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: Full-length atomistic ensembles of the disordered 4E-BP2 in complex with eIF4E, generated by IDPConformerGenerator and restrained by smFRET and NMR data, reveal structural heterogeneity delocalization upon binding — clarifying how cap-dependent translation initiation is regulated by intrinsically disordered binding partners.

papers.title: A curated structural dataset of peptide-protein complexes reveals biases in existing datasets and principles of peptide binding.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: A curated structural dataset of peptide-protein complexes exposes biases in existing databases under the <50 amino acid definition, including miniproteins, peptide-peptide complexes, disulfide-linked artifacts and internal cleavages, and derives principles of peptide binding — informing machine learning, docking and peptide design applications.

papers.title: EvoMut: A computational framework for engineering oxidative stability in proteins.
papers.journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
papers.summary: EvoMut, a computational framework for protein oxidative stability engineering, integrates structural features, local functional context, chemical susceptibility and evolutionary conservation to estimate oxidation risk, explicitly separating oxidation vulnerability from mutation feasibility to identify engineerable sites on therapeutic proteins.

papers.title: Causal Associations Between Plasma Metabolites and Stroke Risk Identified by Mendelian Randomization.
papers.summary: Two-sample Mendelian randomization across 1,400 plasma metabolites and European-ancestry stroke GWAS data identifies 235 nominal associations, with FDR correction and sensitivity analyses revealing causal relationships between specific blood metabolites and stroke risk and its subtypes — pointing to metabolic intervention targets.

papers.title: Predicting Hormesis Effects of GenX in Zebrafish via Interpretable Machine Learning: Insights From SHAP Analysis.
papers.summary: An interpretable machine learning framework — CatBoost master model (AUC 0.977, accuracy 91.25%) across 263 experimental records and 11 biological categories — predicts non-monotonic dose-response (hormesis) of the PFAS alternative GenX in zebrafish, with SHAP analysis identifying effect measurement and biological category as key predictors.

papers.title: C. elegans dauer morphogenesis requires inhibition of DBL-1/BMP signaling by ztf-30.
papers.summary: In C. elegans, the zinc-finger transcription factor ZTF-30 is dispensable for dauer developmental arrest but essential for dauer morphogenesis: mutants form partial dauers lacking protective cuticle and alae, with precocious adult collagen expression and upregulated DBL-1/BMP signaling, consistent with ZTF-30 repressing BMP.

papers.title: Postnatal heart development is coordinated by multi-lineage Wnt and BMP signaling.
papers.summary: Postnatal heart growth transitions from cardiomyocyte proliferation to enlargement and binucleation between postnatal days 3.5-4.5 in mice, with declining beta-catenin and rising SMAD1/5/9 phosphorylation. Multi-lineage Wnt and BMP signaling coordinates this transition, with beta-catenin stabilization enhancing cell-cycle activity while limiting enlargement.

papers.title: Blood flow coordinates collective endothelial cell migration during vascular plexus formation and promotes angiogenic sprout regression via flt4.
papers.summary: In zebrafish, blood flow coordinates collective endothelial cell migration during vascular plexus formation, opposing continuous ventral migration and driving angiogenic sprout regression via flt4, supporting plexus growth and haemodynamically efficient vascular network remodeling.

papers.title: Epigenetic priming and locus-specific demethylation enhance cell-death susceptibility in liver cancer.
papers.summary: Low-dose 5-azacytidine primes liver cancer cells by partially relaxing chromatin at selected loci, restoring silenced cell-death regulators BFL-1 and SQOR. Forced expression increases sensitivity to TNF-alpha/cycloheximide and sorafenib; CRISPR-dCas9-TET1 locus-specific demethylation confirms causality — an epigenetic priming strategy for therapy.

papers.title: Excessive disulfide bonds in lamin A/C contribute to premature human aging.
papers.summary: Lamin A/C mutations R435C and R471C, linked to progeroid syndromes, drive aberrant disulfide cross-linking: R435C facilitates successive intermolecular disulfide bonds between Ig-like domains, while both mutations induce additional bonds involving the lamin A-specific cysteine, contributing to nuclear deformation and premature aging.

papers.title: Conservation of retinal direction-selective circuits across vertebrate species.
papers.summary: Review of direction-selective retinal circuits across vertebrates: shared transcriptional programs diversify DS cell types, molecular cues establish precise synaptic organization, and directional tuning emerges without visual input — a powerful model for dissecting neuronal subtype diversification, neurite guidance and synaptic specificity.

papers.title: Modular Assembly of Systems for Antibody-Directed Enzyme Prodrug Therapy.
papers.summary: A modular plug-and-play approach for antibody-directed enzyme prodrug therapy pairs a self-labeling SNAPtag-enzyme fusion with benzylguanine-tagged antibodies, enabling site-specific antibody-enzyme conjugation with pharmacy-grade antibodies and potential in situ conjugate assembly for improved testing and pharmacokinetics.

papers.title: Genetic divergence and signatures of historical isolation of the traditionally harvested Amolops marmoratus from the Darjeeling Hill Region in the Himalaya Biodiversity Hotspot.
papers.summary: Analysis of 16S rRNA and COI sequences from Amolops marmoratus frogs in the Darjeeling Hill Region (Himalaya Biodiversity Hotspot) reveals low nucleotide and gene diversity locally versus higher diversity in Southeast Asia, China and Myanmar, with elevated F_ST values indicating historical isolation and anthropogenic pressure on this harvested species.

papers.title: Contribution of Topoisomerase IIα chromatin-tether and C-terminal domain to mitotic chromosome association and structural organization.
papers.summary: Topoisomerase II alpha's chromatin-tether domain recognizes methylated chromatin; chimeric swapping between topo II isoforms shows the alpha CHT improves topo II beta's ultrafine DNA bridge resolution but not chromosome bridge prevention, highlighting a requirement for the complete alpha C-terminal domain in accurate chromosome segregation.

papers.title: SET Interacts With CENP-A and HJURP to Ensure Proper Mitotic Progression in Human Cells.
papers.summary: SET, a chromatin-associated protein, was identified as highly enriched in CENP-A immunoprecipitates and associates with both CENP-A and its assembly factor HJURP. Functional studies show SET supports proper centromere assembly and mitotic progression in human cells, extending the regulatory network of centromere inheritance.

papers.title: Fisetin Attenuates Human Macrophage Polarization and Pro-Inflammatory Responses via NLRP3 and NF-κB/MAPK Suppression.
papers.summary: Fisetin, a dietary flavonol, pre-treatment of human THP-1-derived M1 macrophages significantly suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta), ROS production and phagocytic activity via NLRP3 inflammasome and NF-kappaB/MAPK pathway suppression, extending anti-inflammatory evidence to human macrophages.

papers.title: Mechanobiology of Osteoarthritis: Interactions Between Mechanical Stress, Inflammation, and Joint Remodeling.
papers.summary: Review of osteoarthritis mechanobiology: abnormal mechanical stress interacts with inflammation and metabolic pathways to drive joint degeneration. Major mechanosensing mechanisms in chondrocytes — primary cilia, integrins, cytoskeleton, LINC complex, TRPV4/TRPM7/Piezo channels — regulate extracellular matrix homeostasis and chondrocyte function.

papers.title: Synergistic Antitumor Effects and Reduced Systemic Toxicity of Berberine Chloride Combined With Cisplatin in a Female BALB/c Mouse Xenograft Model.
papers.summary: Berberine chloride combined with cisplatin shows synergistic antitumor effects in 4T1 triple-negative breast cancer cells (IC50 ~10 uM and ~2.5 uM respectively) and in a female BALB/c mouse xenograft model, with reduced systemic toxicity versus cisplatin alone — a natural alkaloid chemosensitization strategy.

papers.title: Polymyxin B Attenuates Sepsis-Induced Acute Kidney Injury by Activating a SUMO1-p65 "Molecular Brake" in Kidney Organoids.
papers.summary: Polymyxin B, beyond its antibiotic role, attenuates sepsis-induced acute kidney injury by suppressing NF-kappaB-driven inflammatory programs (CXCL1, IL-6) in 3D mouse kidney organoids via a SUMO1-p65 'molecular brake'; anti-inflammatory efficacy is lost in SUMO1 knockout mice, establishing genetic dependency.

papers.title: β2 Adrenoceptor Signaling Modulates Myoblast Differentiation via miR-374b-5p/GSK3β and miR-326-3p/Tnfrsf11a Axes.
papers.summary: Beta-2 adrenoceptor signaling regulates myoblast differentiation via miR-374b-5p/GSK3beta and miR-326-3p/Tnfrsf11a axes. Knockout myoblasts show decreased differentiation markers; overexpression of these miRNAs rescues fusion index and myogenic gene expression, implicating beta-2 adrenergic-miRNA crosstalk in skeletal muscle regeneration.

papers.title: IGK Suppresses Keloid Fibroblast Activation Through Modulation of MDM2 Expression and p53 Signaling.
papers.summary: Isoginkgetin (IGK) suppresses keloid fibroblast proliferation, migration and activation, inducing cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. MDM2 is elevated in clinical keloid specimens; IGK transcriptionally downregulates MDM2, modulating the MDM2/p53 axis — with eEF1A1 identified as a potential IGK-associated protein via LIP-MS and docking.

papers.title: The Role of Ferroptosis Induced by Iron Overload in Osteoblast and Osteoclast Function.
papers.summary: Iron overload drives ferroptosis in bone cells: ferric ammonium citrate decreases osteoblast viability, downregulates GPX4 and NRF2, increases ROS and lipid peroxidation, and suppresses osteoblastic markers. Ferrostatin-1 restores viability and reduces lipid peroxidation, confirming ferroptosis involvement in iron overload-driven bone loss.

papers.title: Hydrogel-Based Mechano-Immunomodulation in Bone Fracture Healing: Mechanical Regulation of Macrophage Phenotypes, Osteoimmune Interactions, and Regeneration.
papers.summary: Review of hydrogel-based mechano-immunomodulation in bone fracture healing: mechanical cues (strain, stiffness, vibration, topography) regulate macrophage M1-to-M2 polarization via Piezo1, YAP/TAZ and PI3K/AKT pathways, shaping osteoimmune interactions with mesenchymal stem cells, osteoblasts and endothelial cells for regeneration.

papers.title: Potential Protective Effects of Mitochondria-Related Gene EHHADH on Diabetic Cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: EHHADH, a mitochondria-related gene, was identified as a hub differentially expressed gene in diabetic cardiomyopathy. In H9C2 cells, EHHADH protects against apoptosis, lipid accumulation and oxidative stress, with mitochondrial function determined by JC-1 staining and ATP levels; fenofibrate modulates apoptosis protein expression.

papers.title: Organelle scaling over a 100-fold cell size range.
papers.summary: In the polymorphic fungus Aureobasidium pullulans, whose proliferating cells span a ~100-fold volume range, mitochondria and ER scale with cell volume across this range — characterizing how organelle content scales with cell volume far beyond the typical 2-4-fold range, informing organelle biogenesis principles.

papers.title: Organelle partitioning in the multi-budding yeast Aureobasidium pullulans.
papers.summary: Aureobasidium pullulans, a fungus that produces up to 20 daughter cells per cycle, shows even mitochondrial and ER delivery to all growing buds but variable vacuole and peroxisome inheritance — the first characterization of organelle partitioning in a multi-budding organism, with implications for polyextremotolerant growth.

papers.title: Apical actin filament turnover mediated by cyclase-associated protein coordinates non-centrosomal microtubules in epithelium.
papers.summary: In the Drosophila follicular epithelium, loss of cyclase-associated protein (CAP) stabilizes apical actin, causing local microtubule depletion, mislocalization of the crosslinker Shot, and disrupted Patronin localization — showing apical actin turnover coordinates non-centrosomal microtubule organization in epithelial polarity.

papers.title: Setting up for embryogenesis: subcellular changes at the meiosis to mitosis transition.
papers.summary: Review of subcellular remodeling at the meiosis-to-mitosis transition: after fertilization, oocyte asymmetric meiotic divisions give way to symmetric first embryonic mitosis within one cell cycle, with focused changes to spindle, centrosomes and chromosomes enabling the switch to totipotent zygotic division.

papers.title: In vivo clustering of oskar mRNA is driven by RNA concentration, RNA binding proteins, and an RNA palindrome.
papers.summary: In Drosophila embryos, oskar mRNA clustering in vivo is driven by RNA concentration, the dsRNA-binding protein Staufen, and an RNA palindrome promoting dimerization and oligomerization. Oligomerization is more sensitive to perturbation than dimerization, and the palindrome potently drives heterotypic mRNA clustering.

papers.title: Cdk1 and PP2A constitute a molecular switch controlling orderly degradation of atypical E2Fs.
papers.summary: Cdk1 and PP2A constitute a molecular switch controlling orderly APC/C-mediated degradation of atypical E2Fs (E2F7/E2F8), which restrain pro-proliferative E2F1 activity. Flexible N-terminal domains govern phosphorylation-coupled target recognition, coupling cell cycle substrate phosphorylation with ubiquitination and degradation.

papers.title: Stanozolol, an anabolic-androgenic steroid, modulates expression of receptors and disrupts uterine histoarchitecture in Mus musculus.
papers.summary: Stanozolol, an anabolic-androgenic steroid, administered subcutaneously to female mice at 0.5 or 5.0 mg/kg for 30 days, disrupts uterine histoarchitecture and modulates expression of estrogen receptor alpha, androgen receptor and prolactin receptor, with altered serum testosterone and estradiol — documenting reproductive pathophysiology of AAS abuse.

papers.title: CPT1A Ameliorates Staphylococcus aureus-Induced Impairment of the Blood-Milk Barrier and Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress in Mastitis by Promoting NLRP3 Succinylation.
papers.summary: CPT1A is downregulated in Staphylococcus aureus mastitis models in vitro and in vivo; overexpression restores cell viability, mitochondrial membrane potential and blood-milk barrier integrity, ameliorating mitochondrial oxidative stress by promoting NLRP3 succinylation — linking fatty acid oxidation enzyme to mastitis defense.

papers.title: Dapagliflozin Attenuates NKCC2 Protein Expression and Alleviates Diabetic Kidney Disease in Salt Loaded-Hypertensive Diabetic Db/Db Mice.
papers.summary: Dapagliflozin, an SGLT2 inhibitor, attenuates NKCC2 protein expression and alleviates diabetic kidney disease in salt-loaded hypertensive diabetic db/db mice, with metabolic cage urine collection, FITC-sinistrin GFR measurement and tail-cuff blood pressure supporting modulation of tubular sodium transporters and inflammatory pathways.

papers.title: The Underexplored Mechanobiology of Lamin A Biogenesis and Homeostasis.
papers.summary: Review of lamin A mechanobiology: mechanical stimulation dynamically controls lamin A homeostasis through transcriptional, translational and post-translational mechanisms regulating protein abundance, stability and turnover, with emerging evidence that prelamin A maturation may represent a previously unrecognized mechanosensitive regulatory node.

papers.title: USP18 is downregulated in an osteoporosis model and alleviates osteoblast inflammation and apoptosis by deubiquitinating TAK1 to inhibit the MAPK pathway.
papers.summary: USP18 is downregulated in ovariectomy-induced osteoporosis rats and in LPS-stimulated MC3T3-E1 osteoblasts. USP18 alleviates osteoblast inflammation and apoptosis by deubiquitinating TAK1, inhibiting the MAPK pathway — positioning USP18 as a deubiquitinase protecting osteoblasts from inflammatory injury.

papers.title: Angelica sinensis polysaccharide reduces macrophage FPR2 to regulate the hepatic inflammatory microenvironment and activate the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway to improve insulin resistance.
papers.summary: Angelica sinensis polysaccharide reduces macrophage FPR2 to regulate the hepatic inflammatory microenvironment and activate the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway, improving insulin resistance in high-fat diet-fed rats and insulin-treated HepG2 cells, evidenced by glucose/insulin tolerance tests and liver histopathology.
